fol.notes: Multiplication of the numbers asked about is the model's belief, times(x, y): built-in x * y would make the edit contradict arithmetic itself. A firm magnitude rule (|x × y| = |x| · |y|, built-in on the sizes, which nothing changes) gives the size; the sign rule (original or edit) gives the sign. Rules are instantiated over the three products the record asks about. The stored values (−1)(−1) = 1 and (−3)² = 9 give way (top-level gives_up), as q2's and q3's chains state. The square of −3 is asked as times(−3, −3) (the bridge: the square is that product). Negativity of the literals is built-in arithmetic.

magnitude.says: The size of a product is the product of the sizes of its factors.
